title: Cross-functional cycle tradeoff framework and surge roles
creator: Maya Chen
summary: Create a repeatable framework for making scope vs. staffing tradeoffs at cycle planning time, and define a lightweight surge role model (float pool) to preserve critical bets without overcommitting baseline capacity.
background: Redwood's product cycles increasingly need predictable outcomes while balancing spikes in hiring and competing cross-functional demands (Dedicated, Private, runtime optimizations). Current ad-hoc cuts and one-off staff reassignments cause churn, opaque decisions, and missed OKRs. We need a lightweight, actionable playbook that product, eng, and design can use during planning and mid-cycle pivots.
objectives: Provide a single decision rubric teams use during cycle planning to rank scope by customer impact, risk, and unblock probability
Define a surge (float) role model that reserves limited cross-functional capacity for high-confidence escalations without derailing core commitments
Reduce last-minute scope cuts that cascade into downstream QA and docs delays by 30% across two cycles
Document cadence for decisions, required artifacts (PRDs, evals, cost estimates), and escalation paths to PM/EM leads
decision_criteria: Customer impact: high/medium/low and number of customers affected
Operational risk: SLO/regression exposure if not delivered
Opportunity velocity: estimated delta in delivered value per engineering week
Dependency complexity: cross-team touchpoints and external leads required
Cost/infra delta: expected delta in runcost or infra provisioning
proposed_staffing_plan: Baseline allocation: teams plan to 80% of visible capacity (timeboxed) to preserve a 20% buffer for emergent work and bug surges
Float pool definition: 1-2 cross-functional heads per 10 engineers (rotating 6-week assignments), owned by Product Ops but nominally allocated across Eng/Design/SRE
Surge activation policy: PM + EM + Design lead sign-off required; activation timebox 2-6 weeks with explicit success criteria
Backfill rules: when a float is activated for more than 4 weeks, request a hiring requisition or temporary contractor as part of the activation doc
Shadowing/knowledge transfer: each float assignee must produce a 1-page context brief and a 60-minute handoff within 72 hours of activation
staffing_rationale: Empirical evidence from Q4 experiments showed that teams that left a deliberate 15-25% buffer recovered faster from incidents and delivered fewer cascading cuts. The float pool reduces ad-hoc reassignments and reduces context-switching cost by centralizing short-term surge ownership.
scope_tradeoff_matrix: Hard-slices: features critical to launch/OKR that require no scope reduction; cut only if dependency shows unresolvable block
Soft-slices: nice-to-have work that can be deferred with minimal customer impact; prioritize by engineering effort/impact ratio
Timebox-slices: deliver a thinner surface (MVP) within the cycle with clearly documented de-scoped items for next cycle
Fallback-slices: automated mitigations or manual processes to temporarily reduce risk until feature is shipped (e.g., rate limits, gated rollout)
rollout_steps: Draft & align: PMs produce short planning memos per initiative (1-2 pages) with impact, risk, and required FTE
All-hands planning review: triage memos in a 90-minute cross-functional meeting during cycle kickoff
Assign floats: Product Ops publishes float roster and rules the week before cycle start
Decision checkpoints: mid-cycle 2-week review to validate burn and surface activations
Retrospective: capture decisions, misses, and metrics to update playbook for next cycle
metrics: Percentage of cycles with last-minute scope cuts (target <15%)
Time-to-activate float pool from request to assignment (target <7 days)
On-time delivery rate for high-priority OKRs (target 85%+)
Cross-team satisfaction with planning process (pulse survey target >=4/5)
acceptance_criteria: Playbook document published and linked in Planning home (Confluence) with clear activation form
Float roster and activation form implemented as a template in Notion/Confluence
Two pilot teams complete planning using the rubric during next cycle and report results in the retrospective
Product Ops + Eng Managers agree to iterate cadence and staffing ratios after pilot
risks_mitigations: Risk: Float pool becomes permanent headcount sink — Mitigation: strict timeboxing and review before converting to FTE
Risk: PM/EM disagreement on priority — Mitigation: escalation path to Head of Product for tie-break and explicit decision rationale recorded
Risk: Overbooking of buffer capacity across multiple teams — Mitigation: Product Ops enforces baseline 80% planning target and verifies during kickoff
Risk: Knowledge gap when float activates — Mitigation: mandatory 1-page context brief and 60-minute async handoff recorded
dependencies_notes: ENG-2234: runtime batching capacity forecasts needed to evaluate infrastructure-dependent scope
DES-404: final UI direction for rollout toggles and observability UX
Legal: SLA language for Dedicated customers may affect minimum viable scope for some initiatives
notes: This playbook is intentionally light-weight: one page for quick decisions, with a companion appendix for full tradeoff logic. We'll run two pilots (runtime team + console team) and iterate based on observed outcomes.
